answer: On a beacon’s observation horizon, correlated equivocation by k bonded identities incurs slashing across identity pairs, producing a penalty proportional to k(k−1)/2 = O(k²). Asymmetric depreciation compounds escrow losses, so detection of a coordinated sybil swarm applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier; adding identities increases both pairwise liability and compounded downside, even if a walnut-tagged account appears independent.
